Field records indicate that eggs are incubated for an average of 11.5 days [ab = 11.5 days] at a body temperature of 41.6 °C [T = 41.6 °C], after which the altricial nestlings emerge. This rapid embryonic development is consistent with the species' montane distribution, where brief breeding seasons may favor a shortened incubation period to maximize reproductive success before the onset of unfavorable weather. The calculated egg mass aligns well with measurements from other Andean thrushes, suggesting a conserved allometric relationship between egg size and adult body mass across the genus.

This fledging age is typical for thrushes of comparable body size. The attainment of reproductive maturity, defined by the onset of gonadal activity and complete feather replacement, occurs at 37.5 days after hatching [tp = 37.5 days after hatching] under typical thermal conditions of 41.6 °C [T = 41.6 °C].
